# StegaGaussian: Steganography for Asset Generated by 3D Gaussian Splatting

# Introduction
Recently, 3D Gaussian Splatting has emerged as a cutting-edge technique for high-quality 3D scene reconstruction and novel viewpoint synthesis, offering a wide range of applications across various fields. However, compared to traditional visual data such as images and videos, copyright protection for assets generated by 3DGS has not been thoroughly investigated. In this study, we introduce an innovative steganography for 3DGS based on the image frequency domain. By fine-tuning the color attributes of 3DGS using frequency domain, we enable the extraction of watermarks from rendered images to verify the copyright of the model generated by 3DGS. Specifically, we train the 3DGS model using marked images embedded with watermarks and develop an optimization framework to fine-tuning the pre-trained model of 3DGS, aiming to recover watermark information lost during the reconstruction phase. This watermark embedding method ensures that even if the
models generated by 3DGS is misappropriated, the ownership of the digital asset can be determined from the disseminated images. Our method is evaluated across various scenarios, revealing significant insights for practical applications. StegaGaussian represents a pioneering effort in extracting watermarks within images generated by 3DGS, successfully integrating imperceptible yet recoverable information to safeguard both the digital image assets and models generated by 3DGS.

# Highlights
- We propose an innovative steganography method for embedding digital watermarks into models generated by 3DGS. This technique enables direct extraction of watermarks from rendered images for the first time. Even if the model is stolen, the rendered images can still be used to verify copyright ownership.
- We propose a color fine-tuning method based on the frequency domain that adjusts the color of pre-trained 3DGS models. This approach enables the recovery of embedded watermarks without compromising the quality of the reconstruction.
- The embedded watermark demonstrates both high robustness and invisibility;  it remains accurately extractable even if the model is compromised or the rendered images are subjected to various attacks, and the rendered results show no significant visual distortion compared to the version without the watermark.

# Watermark embedding & Extraction
![embed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a48d3d2-454d-4de2-a567-a74cdbbac7ef)

We have written all the scripts we run to the run_scripts.sh. You can run by 

```
./run_scripts.sh --J 2 --alpha 0.1 --lambda 0.2 --dataset [dataset_name]
```

In the context of the DWT (Discrete Wavelet Transform) decomposition, the key parameters are as follows:

- $J$ represents the order of DWT decomposition.
- $\alpha$ denotes the watermark embedding strength.
- &\Lambda& is the ratio between the watermark extraction loss and the scene reconstruction loss.
